bullets.title: NVDA CEO Jensen Huang resigns amid spy scandal; stock down 20%+ from peak
bullets.body: Jensen Huang resigned as NVDA CEO effective immediately following an investigation into his relationship with an executive linked to Chinese intelligence (Alice Huang/Megaspeed), which allegedly facilitated $7.5B+ in chip shipments to China. The board named CFO Colette Kress interim CEO while searching for a permanent successor; DOJ is pursuing multiple probes into NVDA, SMCI, and Megaspeed. Street reaction was bifurcated: retail bought $111M in the first 30 minutes (40x normal volume), multiple sell-side downgrades with PTs cut to $170–$220 range, but bulls argue fundamentals are locked in at ~10x CY27 EPS with demand well ahead of supply.

bullets.title: Export controls tightening; MATCH Act and AI OVERWATCH Act gaining momentum post-scandal
bullets.body: Jensen Huang's departure materially raises the probability of stricter US chip export controls—Commerce is finalizing rules blocking Chinese firms from remote access to advanced AI chips across seven additional countries. Congressional proposals (MATCH Act, AI OVERWATCH Act, Chip Security Act) are advancing toward NDAA inclusion. The 'remote access loophole' through neoclouds in SE Asia provided roughly equivalent compute to smuggled chips; Oracle already cancelled a major Tencent contract under Trump administration pressure.

bullets.title: October CPI/PPI hot; Fed priced for 3 hikes through 2027; 50bp December risk elevated
bullets.body: October core CPI printed +0.30% m/m (third consecutive hot print); PPI headline at 6.5% y/y and core at 5.0% y/y—both cycle highs. Core PCE is tracking ~0.29–0.35% for October depending on the source. Fed Governor Waller said a third straight 0.3% core print puts a 50bp December hike 'on the table'; Dallas Fed's Logan reiterated at least two more hikes possibly at a faster pace. Markets repriced to ~85bp of hikes through end-2027 (up ~39bp w/w), with 13% odds of 50bp in December. Front-end yields posted their biggest weekly increase in two years.

bullets.title: Anthropic IPO at $1.4–1.5T valuation; ~6x oversubscribed; $26B cornerstone placement
bullets.body: Anthropic priced its IPO at $70–$78/share raising ~$61B, with a concurrent $26B private placement from AMD, AVGO, GOOGL, MU, MSFT, NVDA, and TSMC. The deal is reportedly ~6x oversubscribed; $10–15B in passive index demand is expected in the first four weeks post-listing (targeting Nov 19). Revenue run rate was $81B as of Oct 31, though ARR will not hit $100B in 2026; the 2027 target of $130B appears aggressive.

bullets.title: AI infrastructure capex cycle intact post-midterms; ~20% of US DC projects shift 2028→2029
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley, JPMorgan, and Goldman all frame the midterm fallout as a timing delay (5GW shifted from 2028 to 2029) rather than cancellations; 2027 builds are insulated as already funded or under construction. Hyperscaler capex forecasts are unchanged at ~$1.5–1.8T in 2027/2028. Only 2–4% of future data center projects are expected to be cancelled. Texas comprises ~25% of planned capacity and faces the most regulatory risk post-election.

bullets.title: CSCO beats/raises; FY27 AI revenue target raised to $9B (+100% YoY)
bullets.body: Cisco reported F1Q27 revenue of $18.52B (+2.2% vs. consensus), raised FY27 guidance to $74.8–75.8B, and lifted its AI hyperscaler revenue target from $7.5B to $9B—implying 12% of total revenue from AI in FY27 vs. 6% in FY26. Product orders (ex-hyperscalers) decelerated to +14% y/y. The stock faded on order deceleration concerns despite the beat, as gross margins face headwinds from hardware mix shift in 2H FY27.

bullets.title: AMAT beats; 2027 WFE growth guided >30%; cleanroom supply the binding constraint
bullets.body: Applied Materials reported Q4 EPS of $4.16 (+2.5% beat) and guided Q1 to $11.10B (+2.3% above consensus). Management expects 2027 WFE to grow >30% with AMAT outperforming the market; Advanced Packaging grew +90% y/y, Process Control +50% y/y. The company is tracking 20+ fab ramps in CY27; cleanroom availability remains the primary gating factor for supply. GS models ~45% WFE acceleration vs. the 30% management guidance.

bullets.title: NBIS (Nebius) Q3 crushes; FY27 revenue guided $12–13B; capex prepayments cover >100% of Q3 spend
bullets.body: Nebius reported Q3 revenue of $980.8M (8% beat), ARR of $6.4B (36% above consensus), and adjusted EBITDA margins of 47.5% vs. 38.8% expected. GPU pricing rose >20% q/q; new contracts are pricing at >$25M/MW annually. FY27 guidance of $12–13B revenue and $40–45B capex (funded 75–85% by customer prepayments) was well above the $11.7B consensus. Vineland NJ site delays push the $7B+ ARR target to February 2027.

bullets.title: CoreWeave beats; capacity sold out through 2027; self-funding path de-risks balance sheet
bullets.body: CRWV reported Q3 revenue of $3.66B (+168% y/y, 300bp beat), with non-GAAP operating margins of 10% (ahead of plan by one quarter). Q4 is guided to ~16% OM. GPU pricing rose ~25–35% in Q3; short-term contracts command >$40M/MW annually; 2027 renewals (~130K GPUs) represent ~$4B incremental annualized revenue with no additional capex. Management expects <$5B in parent-level equity raises through 2027 and no unsecured debt; next DDTL expected at 7–7.5% yield.

bullets.title: Semis positioning at multi-year lows; SOX P/E at 13x matches historical trough; AMD/AVGO gain on NVDA
bullets.body: The SOX index fell ~30% from its June peak with 70% of constituents near DeMark buy signals. AMD gained +40% over four days and AVGO +5–6% as investors rotated away from NVDA. The semiconductor forward P/E fell to 13.4x (matching historical downturn median), well below the post-2011 average of 18.6x. Goldman notes AI/datacenter downside is largely priced into electronics/test stocks (APH, KEYS, TEL, BDC) with upside in downside scenarios.

bullets.title: Memory super-cycle: HBM sold out through 2027; enterprise SSD prices rising 15–20% q/q
bullets.body: Memory manufacturers are planning 15–20% sequential enterprise SSD price increases in Q4 2026; PC DRAM prices are rising 13–18% q/q despite weaker consumer demand. SK Hynix achieved mid-60% HBM4 yields; Samsung will produce HBM base dies for AMD and NVDA at its Texas fab. DRAM spot-price premiums of 30–50% have emerged, with shortages expected through 2027. 2026 represents a $200B DRAM super-cycle per multiple sell-side estimates.

bullets.title: Housing slump deepens; existing home sales at 2010 lows; mortgage rates highest since 2000
bullets.body: Existing home sales fell 5.5% m/m to 3.75M annualized in October—the lowest level since 2010 and matching GFC lows. Single-family sales are 27% below population-adjusted historical norms. Mortgage rates are at their highest since 2000 (excluding one month in 2023); median home prices rose only 0.4% y/y, the smallest gain since February. Housing recovery requires both lower Treasury yields and lower rate volatility.

bullets.title: Global REITs outperformed tech by 14.9ppts during October's IT sector drawdown
bullets.body: Global REITs returned +6.6% over the month to November 5 while the S&P 500 IT Index fell -16.5%. The FTSE EPRA Nareit Developed Index has historically outperformed tech by 14.9ppts during IT sector drawdowns >10% since 1990. Self-storage and Hong Kong were top-performing sub-sectors; US apartment new lease rent growth accelerated materially in October with both coastal markets and Sunbelt pricing improving.

bullets.title: FOXA becomes Top Pick at Morgan Stanley post-Roku deal close; $90 PT implies 37% upside
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley resumed Overweight coverage and elevated FOXA to Top Pick following the early close of the $22B Roku acquisition. Pro forma revenue growth lifts to ~6% (from low-single digits), EBITDA CAGR rises to ~9% (from ~1%), and FCF per share compounds at ~20% through FY30. The combined Fox/Tubi/Roku Channel holds 10%+ of monthly US TV viewing, rivaling Disney and ahead of Netflix; $400M+ in cost synergies are modeled with $500M–$1B revenue synergy potential excluded from base case.

bullets.title: Hyperscaler AI capex now 40% of new LT debt issuance; crowding out effect widening spreads
bullets.body: Hyperscalers now represent 40% of new long-term IG debt issuance vs. historically a rounding error. YTD USD high-grade issuance totals $232B for hyperscalers and $42B for data centers; asset managers own 53% and 79% of these respectively. Rising interest expense is an emerging risk as mega-cap tech draws down cash to finance AI capex, with 2027 IG TMT issuance forecast at $675B ($450B AI-related). Citi flags this as a potential drag on forward EPS estimates.

bullets.title: ChatGPT Ads hit $1B ARR with 10K advertisers; Pinterest identified as clearest share donor
bullets.body: OpenAI's ChatGPT advertising business reached ~$1B annualized run rate by August 2026, growing from ~600 to 10,000+ advertisers in seven months. ROI perception is rated middling (in line with Pinterest/Nextdoor, below Google/Instagram/TikTok). Only 11% of agencies are buying ChatGPT ads; Pinterest is the clearest share donor with more agencies planning to cut vs. add spend there in 2026–2027. The key open question is whether ChatGPT dollars represent new spend or reallocation from GOOGL/META/AMZN.

bullets.title: UK GDP outperforms at 3% annualized; BoE likely to hike in December on sticky inflation
bullets.body: UK Q3 GDP rose 0.7% q/q (3% annualized), with JPMorgan raising the Q4 forecast to 1.5% annualized. October headline CPI is expected to accelerate to 3.8% y/y; natural gas prices rebounded, reducing the case for the BoE to wait until February. JPMorgan forecasts inflation will not drop below 4% until September 2027; food inflation is expected to peak above 4% annually by next summer. RICS housing shows accelerating price weakness.

bullets.title: HUBS co-founder Halligan returns as CEO; company in 're-founding' mode
bullets.body: HubSpot co-founder Brian Halligan returned as CEO effective November 12, replacing Yamini Rangan, in what management described as a 're-founding' across product, go-to-market, and culture. CFO Kate Bueker is retiring; Adobe's Karen Burgess joins as CFO. Q4 and FY26 guidance were reaffirmed. The move follows similar co-founder returns at Workday (Bhusri); JPM views the announcement as positive, expecting it to address expansion rate pressures and AI monetization execution.

bullets.title: Agentic commerce reaching inflection; AMZN/META/GOOGL racing to control AI-driven product discovery
bullets.body: Citi sees agentic commerce as a material contributor to eCommerce growth in 2027, with AI-referred shoppers converting ~48% better than other traffic sources. AMZN is building a 'World Product Graph' and has 400M+ Alexa Shopping users; META's Muse has scaled to 10M US/Canada users and was blocked by eBay and United Airlines. GOOGL's AI Mode prompts are 3x longer than traditional search, capturing richer intent. Consumer data and memory integration are cited as the core competitive moat.

bullets.title: Technical deterioration: AI + semis expected to work lower; NYSE/Nasdaq breadth weak; 53-day streak of new lows outnumbering highs
bullets.body: Technical analysis shows the NASDAQ has recorded new lows outnumbering new highs for 53 consecutive days (69 consecutive days with at least 100 new lows) despite only a ~12% correction. The percentage of stocks above their 200-day moving average signals the market is not oversold. CTAs flipped net short global equities from +150% to -5% exposure. The sell-side notes the AI/memory/semis complex is expected to work lower, with the market having not fully cleared despite multiple de-risking events (hedge fund de-grossing, midterms, NVDA CEO resignation).
